roadbuilder.row.hint: Choose the object that stands in a row along the lane, such as a tree or a street light. It is laid whenever the road type is built.
roadbuilder.row.panel: Click the object for lane {lane}; Esc goes back to the road builder.
roadbuilder.status.pick_row: Road builder: click the object for lane {lane} in the library, such as a tree or, under Lights, a street light.
roadbuilder.status.row_set: Road builder: a row of {name} stands along lane {lane} whenever the road type is built{turned, select, yes {, turned by {degrees, number, 0}° so it runs along the road} other {}}; set how far apart and where across the lane.
@roadbuilder.status.row_set: {turned} is yes or no and chooses a part: keep it in English
roadbuilder.rows_laid: {count, plural, one {# object stands} other {# objects stand}} in rows along it.
@roadbuilder.rows_failed: {list} names the objects, separated by commas
roadbuilder.rows_kept: {name} (a row of it there is still needed)
roadbuilder.bus_failed: The bus lanes could not be kept for buses: {reason}
@roadbuilder.bus_failed: {reason} is a message from the system, in English
roadbuilder.status.start: Road builder: pick a lane in the bar to change it, add lanes or start from a template, then save the road type.
roadbuilder.status.make_failed: Road builder: the road type could not be made: {reason}
@roadbuilder.status.make_failed: {reason} is a message from the system, in English
roadbuilder.status.made: Road builder: made {name} ({width, number, 0.00} m) as {path} in your OMSI installation; it is chosen in the road tool, click on the map to build it.
@roadbuilder.status.unreadable: {reason} is a message from the system, in English
roadbuilder.status.no_lanes: Road builder: {name} holds no lanes the road builder can read; it was not made with it.
roadbuilder.status.edit: Road builder: change {name} and save it; {uses, plural, =0 {no spline of this map uses it yet.} one {the spline of it in this map changes with it.} other {all # splines of it in this map change with it.}}
roadbuilder.status.change_failed: Road builder: {name} could not be changed: {reason}
@roadbuilder.status.change_failed: {reason} is a message from the system, in English
roadbuilder.status.changed: Road builder: changed {name} ({width, number, 0.00} m){uses, plural, =0 {} one {; # spline of it changed with it} other {; # splines of it changed with it}}{remade, plural, =0 {} one {, # junction was made again{every, select, yes { with every way through, as the lanes changed} other {}}} other {, # junctions were made again{every, select, yes { with every way through, as the lanes changed} other {}}}}{hasStayed, select, yes {; these junctions stay as they were: {stayed}} other {}}{rows, plural, =0 {} one {; # object stands in its rows} other {; # objects stand in its rows}}{hasFailed, select, yes {; not laid: {failed}} other {}}. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
@roadbuilder.status.changed: {every}, {hasStayed} and {hasFailed} are yes or no and choose parts of the sentence: keep them in English; {stayed} and {failed} are lists
roadbuilder.problem.mismatch: its connection points do not match its file
roadbuilder.problem.keep: the roads at it cannot be kept as they are
roadbuilder.problem.references: {references} still need it as it is
roadbuilder.status.stays_splines: Road builder: {name} stays; {uses, plural, one {# spline of this map uses it.} other {# splines of this map use it.}}
roadbuilder.status.looking: Road builder: looking whether any map or made junction still uses {name}...
roadbuilder.status.look_failed: Road builder: {name} stays; looking for what uses it failed: {reason}
@roadbuilder.status.look_failed: {reason} is a message from the system, in English
roadbuilder.status.stays_named: Road builder: {name} stays; {users} still names it.{made, select, yes { Delete unused made objects in the map check first.} other {}}
@roadbuilder.status.stays_named: {users} is a file or map name; {made} is yes or no and chooses a part: keep it in English
roadbuilder.status.delete_failed: Road builder: {name} could not be deleted: {reason}
@roadbuilder.status.delete_failed: {reason} is a message from the system, in English
roadbuilder.status.deleted: Road builder: deleted {name} from your OMSI installation; its textures stay for the other road types. Ctrl+Z brings it back.
roadbuilder.status.nothing_to_split: Road builder: {name} has no carriageway or footpath to take apart into lanes.
roadbuilder.status.split: Road builder: took {name} apart into {count, plural, one {# lane} other {# lanes}}, {width, number, 0.00} m wide, with lines and surfaces of the builder{hasNotes, select, yes {. {notes}} other {.}}
@roadbuilder.status.split: {notes} are remarks of MapWorks in English
@roadbuilder.panel.edit: {name} is the name of the road type, shown unchanged
roadbuilder.panel.name.tooltip_new: The name of the road type, also its file name under Splines\Mapforge in your OMSI installation
roadbuilder.panel.name.tooltip_edit: The name for Save as new type; Save keeps the road type under its name
roadbuilder.panel.save_as_new.tooltip: Makes a road type of its own under the name typed; the one edited stays as it was
roadbuilder.panel.save.tooltip_new: Makes the road type and chooses it in the road tool, ready to build
roadbuilder.panel.save.tooltip_edit: Changes {name}: {uses, plural, one {the spline} other {all # splines}} of it in this map and the junctions made with it change too; Ctrl+Z undoes it
roadbuilder.panel.delete.tooltip_free: Deletes {name} from your OMSI installation, unless another map or a made junction still uses it; Ctrl+Z brings it back
roadbuilder.panel.delete.tooltip_used: No spline of this map may use {name} to delete it; {uses} still do
roadbuilder.panel.close.tooltip: Back to the road picker without saving (Esc)
roadbuilder.panel.add_title: Add a lane right of the one picked
roadbuilder.panel.add_tooltip: Adds a lane right of the lane picked: {lane}
roadbuilder.panel.from_chosen.tooltip_on: Takes {name}, the road chosen in the road tool, apart into lanes to start from

roadbuilder.panel.pick_title: Pick a lane or the line between two in the bar above
roadbuilder.panel.forward.tooltip: Traffic runs the way the road is drawn
roadbuilder.panel.backward.tooltip: Traffic runs against the way the road is drawn
roadbuilder.panel.surface.tooltip: Choose a texture of your installation's spline profiles for the lane

roadbuilder.panel.standard.tooltip_click: The base game's texture for this kind of lane; click to choose another
roadbuilder.panel.tram_only.tooltip: A track of its own, kept apart from cars with a solid line
roadbuilder.panel.cars_too.tooltip: Tracks laid in the street: cars and buses drive on them too
roadbuilder.panel.objects.tooltip: Choose a tree, a street light or any object in the library; a row of it is laid along the lane whenever the road is built
roadbuilder.panel.turn.tooltip: Degrees the objects are turned by, clockwise; 90 lays a hedge modelled across along the road
roadbuilder.panel.move_left.tooltip: Moves the lane one place left; you can also drag it in the bar
roadbuilder.panel.move_right.tooltip: Moves the lane one place right; you can also drag it in the bar
roadbuilder.panel.auto.tooltip: The line the editor chooses, as on German roads
roadbuilder.panel.line_hint: A line at a kerb lies 0.2 m out on the carriageway, as an edge line.
roadbuilder.panel.back.tooltip: Back to the lane without changing its surface
roadbuilder.panel.surface.open_map: Open a map to choose from its installation's textures.
roadbuilder.panel.surface.reading: Reading the textures of the installation's spline profiles...
roadbuilder.panel.surface.none: The installation's spline profiles use no textures.
roadbuilder.panel.summary: {count, plural, one {# lane} other {# lanes}}, {width, number, 0.00} m wide

roadbuilder.panel.marking.broad.tooltip: Broad solid line, as beside bus and bike lanes

roadbuilder.panel.place.kerb.tooltip: By the kerb, or the side towards the road, 0.75 m in
roadbuilder.panel.place.middle.tooltip: In the middle of the lane
roadbuilder.panel.place.outer.tooltip: At the side away from the road, 0.75 m in
